title.analysis: Authentic title "$100,000 Means You're 1/3 Of The Way To $1,000,000 (The Surprising Math)" is a counterintuitive-math frame. The script delivers it as elapsed time (12 of about 36 years at $100 a week and 8%), not as money; the title reads as a money claim, so the "one-third" holds only under the time interpretation.

script.opening_words: Have you ever stared at your investment account balance and wondered if you're making any real progress toward building wealth? Maybe you've got a few thousand dollar saved up or perhaps you've been grinding away for years and finally hit 20 or 30,000. Either way, that million dollar milestone feels impossibly far away, doesn't it? Well, what if I told you that once you reach $100,000, you're already closer to becoming a millionaire than you might think. In fact, you'd
script.ending_words: milestone on your way to becoming a millionaire. It's actually proof that you're already onethird of the way there. The math doesn't lie, even if it seems almost too good to be true. Time and compound interest are working in your favor, but only if you give them the chance. Start investing consistently today because 36 years from now, you'll either be thanking yourself or wondering what could have been.
script.analysis: Full 19596 canonical characters read. A single-narrator compound-interest explainer: hook on stalled balances, linear-vs-exponential framing, a $100-a-week at 8% walk-through (12, 18, 36 and 45 years), objections (inflation, crashes, affordability with food and car examples), the psychology of the first $100,000 and Munger, opportunity value, delayed gratification, conservative-assumption caveats, index-fund advice and a closing call to start now. The timeline arithmetic reproduces; the money-vs-time framing of "one-third" and "halfway" and the "8% is inflation-adjusted and conservative" claim are misleading.
